ev.d_rumor.title: Whispers at the Well
ev.d_rumor.text: The neighbor women at the well fall silent whenever you come near. At last one of them whispers: {npc} has been calling on {g=npc_sex:a certain young widow|a certain cloth merchant} far too often. Maybe it's only spiteful tongues…
ev.d_rumor.ask.success: {npc} flushed at first, then burst out laughing: the wool there is simply cheaper. You no longer believe the gossips.
ev.d_rumor.ask.failure: {npc} was silent for a long time, then turned to face the wall. That silence was the answer.
ev.d_rumor.follow.success: You spent half a day hiding round a corner and saw nothing but {npc} haggling over pots. Embarrassing — but your heart is light.
ev.d_rumor.follow.failure: The gossip was true. You saw it with your own eyes and walked away without a word.
ev.d_rumor.ignore.ok: You decided that other people's tongues have no place in your house. But a worm of doubt remained.
ev.d_unfaithful.title: Betrayal
ev.d_unfaithful.text: There's no doubt left: {npc} has been unfaithful to you. {g=npc_sex:He|She} makes no excuses and waits for your word. Even the house has gone quiet, as if listening.
ev.d_unfaithful.forgive.ok: You forgave. Not at once and not completely — but you sit at the same table again.
ev.d_unfaithful.divorce.ok: {g:You sent her back to her family with her dowry, as custom demands.|You took back your dowry and returned to your own people.} The house is empty, but it's easier to breathe.
ev.d_unfaithful.divorce.ok.rome: {g:You said before witnesses, 'Take what's yours and go' — in Rome that's enough.|You declared the divorce yourself — in Rome a wife has that right too — and took back your dowry.} The house is empty, but it's easier to breathe.
ev.d_unfaithful.divorce.ok.athens: {g:You sent her back to her family with her dowry, as the law requires.|You lodged your declaration with the archon, as the law requires, and returned to your family with your dowry.} The house is empty, but it's easier to breathe.
ev.d_unfaithful.confront: Have it out with the {g=npc_sex:other woman|seducer}
ev.d_unfaithful.confront.success: You made such a scene that the {g=npc_sex:other woman|seducer} won't come near your house again. {npc} is ashamed and quiet.
ev.d_unfaithful.confront.failure: The scene ended in a brawl, a night in custody and a fine. Now the whole quarter knows the story.
ev.d_unfaithful.apart: Share a roof, but live apart
ev.d_unfaithful.apart.ok: You share a house, a household and a name — but not a bed. The neighbors needn't know.
ev.d_old_secret.title: An Old Truth
ev.d_old_secret.text: Many years later an old neighbor let it slip: that gossip at the well had been true. {npc} has long since become a different person — but now you know.
ev.d_old_secret.let_go: Let the past stay in the past
ev.d_old_secret.let_go.ok: You put that truth where old grudges lie — at the very bottom. Life goes on.
ev.d_old_secret.talk.success: You talked until dawn. Honestly, for the first time in years.
ev.d_old_secret.talk.failure: The old wound opened again, and words only made it worse.
ev.d_old_secret.divorce.ok: Many shook their heads: so many years have passed. But you decided you would not live with it.
ev.d_late_peace.title: The Scar Has Healed
ev.d_late_peace.text: One evening {npc} took your hand, as in your first year together. That old trouble has become simply part of your shared story — a scar that no longer hurts.
ev.d_cold_house.title: Strangers Under One Roof
ev.d_cold_house.text: Years under one roof — and apart. {npc} still goes out in the evenings, and you still pretend not to notice. How long can this go on?
ev.d_cold_house.divorce.ok: The divorce took one day. You were surprised how few things turned out to be truly yours.
ev.d_cold_house.endure: Endure, as others endured before you
ev.d_cold_house.endure.ok: You bring cakes to the temple and keep silent. The gods are patient — so must you be.
ev.d_cold_house.own_life.ok: You started going out in the evenings yourself — to friends, to festivals, to the shore. The neighbors talk, but for the first time in years you feel light.
ev.d_temptation.title: First Love
ev.d_temptation.text: {g:The girl|The boy} you dreamed of in your youth has come back to town — widowed now, still laughing with {g:her|his} eyes alone. The meetings by the fountain grow longer, and at home {npc} asks why you're so late.
ev.d_temptation.affair.ok: You feel twenty years younger. And you're lying as never before in your life.
ev.d_temptation.farewell.ok: You said goodbye at the same fountain. At home, {npc} wondered why you held {g=npc_sex:him|her} so tightly.
ev.d_temptation.friends.success: You learned to be friends. Sometimes that's even easier than loving.
ev.d_temptation.friends.failure: The friendship didn't work: too many glances, too few words. {npc} noticed everything.
ev.d_affair_found.title: The Note
ev.d_affair_found.text: {npc} found a note you should never have kept. There was only one question: 'How long?'
ev.d_affair_found.confess.success: You were forgiven — on a condition you'll remember all your life.
ev.d_affair_found.confess.failure: {npc} packed that same evening. The door closed quietly, and that quiet was worse than shouting.
ev.d_affair_found.deny.success: You were believed. Or {npc} pretended to believe you.
ev.d_affair_found.deny.failure: The lie came out within a week, and that turned out worse than the affair itself.
ev.d_affair_found.leave.ok: You walked out with a single bundle. Half the town condemns you; the other half envies you.
ev.d_jealous.title: Jealousy
ev.d_jealous.text: {npc} is jealous of everyone: of the {g:neighbor woman with the water jar|potter next door}, of your {g:women customers|customers}, even of the old writing master. Yesterday it came to broken dishes.
ev.d_jealous.soothe.ok: Again and again you explained that {g=npc_sex:he is|she is} the only one you love. It helped — until next time.
ev.d_jealous.snap: Give as good as you get
ev.d_jealous.snap.ok: You broke a couple of pots too. Now the house has two jealous people and not a single whole jug.
ev.d_jealous.temple.success: The priest heard you both and told you to make a single offering together. On the way home you held hands for the first time in a month.
ev.d_jealous.temple.failure: The priest talked at length, but {npc} only half listened and spent the whole way home glaring at passers-by.
ev.d_jealous_scene.title: A Scene at the Market
ev.d_jealous_scene.text: {npc} made a scene right in the middle of the market, in front of everyone — over a trivial chat with the fig seller. People laughed about it until evening.
ev.d_jealous_scene.divorce.ok: You walked away from the market — and from that marriage. The gossips talked and then forgot.
ev.d_jealous_scene.reconcile.success: That evening {npc} wept and asked forgiveness. Since then the jealousy has cooled.
ev.d_jealous_scene.reconcile.failure: The talk ended in another quarrel. The neighbors no longer even listen — they're used to it.
ev.d_jealous_scene.endure.ok: You silently picked up the spilled figs. But you take a different road to the market now.
ev.d_gambler.title: The Empty Chest
ev.d_gambler.text: The chest where you kept money for a rainy day is nearly empty. {npc} confesses: dice, a tavern debt — 'one more throw and I'd have won it all back.'
ev.d_gambler.pay: Cover the debt and forget it
ev.d_gambler.pay.ok: You paid off the tavern keeper. {npc} swears never again. You very much want to believe it.
ev.d_gambler.purse: Take the key to the chest
ev.d_gambler.purse.ok: The key hangs at your belt now. {npc} sulks, but the money has stopped vanishing.
ev.d_gambler.oath: Take {g=npc_sex:him|her} to the altar to swear an oath
ev.d_gambler.oath.success: At the altar {npc} swore never to touch dice again — and seems to be keeping the oath.
ev.d_gambler.oath.failure: The oath was sworn, the offering made. A month later you found the purse short again.
ev.d_gambler.divorce: Divorce while there's something left to save
ev.d_gambler.divorce.ok: You took what was left and walked out. Living poor but in peace is a life too.
ev.d_gambler_again.title: Men with an IOU
ev.d_gambler_again.text: Two burly men from a gambling den stand in the doorway, holding an IOU. The name signed at the bottom: {npc}.
ev.d_gambler_again.pay.ok: You counted out the coins without meeting anyone's eye. The chest is empty again.
ev.d_gambler_again.throw_out.success: You stood in the doorway so fiercely that they backed off. Those two never came again.
ev.d_gambler_again.throw_out.failure: They came back at night — four of them this time. The debt had to be paid with interest, and the bruises took a month to fade.
ev.d_gambler_again.divorce.ok: You declared you'd answer for no one else's debts and left. Let the dice feed the gambler.
ev.d_sp_illness.title: The Fever
ev.d_sp_illness.text: {npc} has taken to bed with a fever. For three days {g=npc_sex:he has|she has} barely opened {g=npc_sex:his|her} eyes, and the neighbor women are already whispering about bad omens.
ev.d_sp_illness.physician.success: The physician gave bitter draughts and ordered the windows kept open. On the seventh day the fever broke.
ev.d_sp_illness.physician.failure: The physician did all he could. Towards morning {npc} quietly fell asleep — and never woke.
ev.d_sp_illness.temple: Pray and bring offerings to the temple
ev.d_sp_illness.temple.success: Coming back from the temple, you heard a weak voice: {npc} was asking for water. The gods had listened.
ev.d_sp_illness.temple.failure: This time the gods were silent. {npc} passed at dawn, holding your hand.
ev.d_sp_illness.nurse.success: You didn't sleep for nine nights, changing the wet cloths. On the tenth day {npc} smiled.
ev.d_sp_illness.nurse.failure: You did everything you could. But the illness was stronger.
ev.d_sp_drowned.title: The River
ev.d_sp_drowned.text: The boat {npc} was crossing the river in overturned in the rapids. The river gave {g=npc_sex:him|her} back only on the third day. The house is full of people, yet it feels empty to you.
ev.d_sp_drowned.text.athens: {npc} was sailing to Salamis in a small boat when a squall struck. The sea gave {g=npc_sex:him|her} back only on the third day. The house is full of people, yet it feels empty to you.
ev.d_sp_drowned.mourn.ok: You kept every rite, day after day. They gave you something to hold on to.
ev.d_sp_drowned.work.ok: You worked from dark to dark so as not to be alone with the silence.
ev.d_sp_drowned.friends.ok: Friends brought food, sat beside you and kept silent with you. It was enough to get through to spring.
ev.d_grief_year.title: A Year Later
ev.d_grief_year.text: A year has passed. You still set out an extra cup out of habit, but one morning you catch yourself smiling at the sun. The pain hasn't gone — it has only grown quieter.
ev.d_grief_year.return: Allow yourself to go on living
ev.d_grief_year.return.ok: You put off mourning and went to a festival for the first time in a year. It was noisy — and that was good.
ev.d_grief_year.remember.ok: Every month you bring wine and flowers to the tomb. Talking with the departed keeps you on your feet too.
ev.d_grief_year.help: Help others who have lost someone
ev.d_grief_year.help.ok: You became the one neighbors turn to on dark days. Sharing others' grief lightens your own.
ev.d_t_spouse_accused.title: The Accusation
ev.d_t_spouse_accused.text: At dawn the watch came: {npc} stands accused of stealing silver from the house where {g=npc_sex:he worked|she helped with the household}. A witness swears he saw it all himself. The trial is in nine days.
ev.d_t_spouse_accused.advocate.success: The advocate tore the witness's story to shreds: that night he'd been drinking on the other side of town. {npc} was acquitted.
ev.d_t_spouse_accused.advocate.failure: Even an expensive advocate didn't help. The court believed the witness, and {npc} stays in custody until the penalty is paid.
ev.d_t_spouse_accused.bribe.success: The witness suddenly 'remembered' he was mistaken. The case was dropped. You try not to think about whether you did right.
ev.d_t_spouse_accused.bribe.failure: The witness took the money — and promptly told the judge about it. Now you're both under suspicion.
ev.d_t_spouse_accused.defend.success: You spoke plainly and firmly, and the judges believed you: {npc} is free, and your speech was talked about in the streets for a long time.
ev.d_t_spouse_accused.defend.failure: Your voice shook and your words tangled. The court wasn't convinced, and {npc} remains in custody.
ev.d_t_spouse_accused.disown: Divorce to keep your own name clean
ev.d_t_spouse_accused.disown.ok: You announced the divorce before the trial. Your name is clean — but at night you lie awake for a long time.
ev.d_sp_back.title: The Return
ev.d_sp_back.text: {npc} has come home after long months in custody — thin and silent. The neighbors cross to the other side of the street.
ev.d_sp_back.stand_by.ok: On the very first day you walked together through the whole market without lowering your eyes. The whispers died down in time.
ev.d_sp_back.fresh_start.ok: You sold the house at a loss and moved where no one knows you. The new neighbors greet you first.
ev.d_sp_back.distance.ok: You live under one roof, but now there's a wall between you that nobody built.
ev.d_ex_meeting.title: Many Years Later
ev.d_ex_meeting.text: At the market you came face to face with the {g:woman|man} you once shared a home and a bed with. Both of you have more grey hair now, and somehow the old grudges don't come to mind.
ev.d_ex_meeting.talk.ok: You talked until the market closed — about prices, old neighbors, how everything has changed. You parted almost as friends.
ev.d_ex_meeting.pass.ok: You nodded to each other like old acquaintances. The past stayed in the past.
ev.d_ex_meeting.help: Help with money — life has clearly been hard
ev.d_ex_meeting.help.ok: You quietly pressed a purse into a hand. 'Just like old times,' came the reply, with a faint smile.
ev.d_remarry.title: Matchmakers Again
ev.d_remarry.text: You're on your own again, and the matchmakers haven't forgotten. One offers a {g:widow with a solid household|widower with a big house}; another, a {g:neighbor of modest means who's quick to laugh|craftsman of modest means with a kind heart} you sometimes think about yourself.
ev.d_remarry.practical.ok: The household grew stronger, the evenings calmer. Love may come later.
ev.d_remarry.heart.ok: Less money, more laughter. The second time you chose for yourself — and you don't regret it.
ev.d_remarry.alone.ok: You're {g:master|mistress} of your house and your days. Lonely sometimes — but quiet.
ev.d_new_love.title: A New Feeling
ev.d_new_love.text: After everything, you didn't think your heart could still beat like this. But the {g:potter's widow|widowed potter} from the next street smiles at you every morning — and you catch yourself waiting for that smile.
ev.d_new_love.court.success: You married quietly, without fuss — like people who know the worth of both happiness and loss.
ev.d_new_love.court.failure: {g:She|He} gently declined: {g:her|his} own wounds are still too fresh. You understand — and it hurts all the same.
ev.d_new_love.slow.ok: You simply greet each other in the mornings and sometimes walk to the market together. Let time decide.
ev.d_new_love.no.ok: You started taking another road to the market. Not now. Maybe never.
ev.d_inlaws.title: The In-Laws
ev.d_inlaws.text: The family you married into still treats you as an outsider. At every festival your mother-in-law recalls aloud the fine {g:suitors|brides} who came calling before, and {npc} pretends not to hear.
ev.d_inlaws.gifts.ok: Fine wine and an embroidered shawl did the trick: at the next feast they called you 'one of ours' for the first time.
ev.d_inlaws.stand.success: You answered so calmly and with such dignity that the table fell silent. No one mentions the old matches anymore.
ev.d_inlaws.stand.failure: It came out sharper than you meant. The feast ended in a quarrel, and {npc} didn't speak to you for a week.
ev.d_inlaws.choose.success: {npc} stood up and said in front of everyone: 'This is my family.' The relatives went quiet.
ev.d_inlaws.choose.failure: {npc} couldn't go against {g=npc_sex:his|her} own people. A crack opened between you.
ev.d_inlaws.cut.ok: Now you spend the festivals just the two of you. Quieter, plainer — and calmer.
ev.d_inlaws_need.title: Fire at the In-Laws'
ev.d_inlaws_need.text: A messenger came running in the night: there's been a fire at the house of those same difficult in-laws. {npc} looks at you in silence, not daring to ask.
ev.d_inlaws_need.help: Take them in and help them rebuild
ev.d_inlaws_need.help.ok: For six months the house was cramped and loud. But now your mother-in-law is the first to rise when you walk in.
ev.d_inlaws_need.refuse.ok: You remembered every feast and every barb — and didn't give a single coin. {npc} won't forget it.
ev.d_son_brawl.title: Taken by the Watch
ev.d_son_brawl.text: Pounding on the door at night: {npc} has been taken by the watch {g=npc_sex:after a tavern brawl — the other man still can't get up|on a charge of stealing a bracelet from a market stall}. In the morning the case goes before the magistrate.
ev.d_son_brawl.fine: Pay the injured party and the fine
ev.d_son_brawl.fine.ok: You paid everyone who needed paying. You walked home in silence, and that silence was louder than any reproach.
ev.d_son_brawl.lesson: Let {g=npc_sex:him|her} sit there — maybe it'll teach a lesson
ev.d_son_brawl.lesson.ok: You didn't go to the magistrate. Let {g=npc_sex:him|her} answer for what was done.
ev.d_son_brawl.patron: Ask an influential acquaintance to intervene
ev.d_son_brawl.patron.success: One word from the right man and the case was hushed up. Now you owe him.
ev.d_son_brawl.patron.failure: The acquaintance spread his hands: not this time. The case took its course.
ev.d_son_released.title: Home Again
ev.d_son_released.text: {npc} came back from custody a different person: sullen looks, leaving after dark, and new friends best not asked about.
ev.d_son_released.work: Take {g=npc_sex:him|her} into your work and keep watch
ev.d_son_released.work.ok: Every morning now you start work together. Through gritted teeth at first, then out of habit.
ev.d_son_released.harsh.ok: Rules, reproaches, a locked door. {npc} obeys — for now.
ev.d_son_released.away: Send {g=npc_sex:him|her} to friends in the country, away from bad company
ev.d_son_released.away.ok: Country air, hard work and not a tavern within a day's walk. We'll see.
ev.d_son_redeemed.title: By Honest Work
ev.d_son_redeemed.text: {npc} came to you with a first purse of honestly earned coins: 'This is for everything you did for me back then.' You didn't take a single coin — but you'll remember that day forever.
ev.d_son_criminal.title: Bad Company
ev.d_son_criminal.text: The watch is hunting a gang that's been robbing the harbor warehouses, and among the names given is {npc}. In the middle of the night, {g=npc_sex:he|she} is standing on your doorstep.
ev.d_son_criminal.hide.success: The watch searched half the quarter but didn't come to your door. A month later it all blew over.
ev.d_son_criminal.hide.failure: The watch found the hiding place. Now you're called an accomplice too.
ev.d_son_criminal.hand_over.ok: It was the hardest walk of your life. But at least you know: what comes next is a trial, not a knife in an alley.
ev.d_son_criminal.repay.ok: You went round every victim with money and bows. The case never reached court.
ev.d_elope.title: Eloped
ev.d_elope.text: {npc} ran off in the night {g=npc_sex:with a girl from the next street|with a young mule driver}, leaving only a note. The whole quarter is waiting to see what you'll do.
ev.d_elope.bless: Give your blessing — what else is there?
ev.d_elope.bless.ok: You sent a messenger after them with gifts and your blessing. The neighbors gossiped for a week, then found something new to talk about.
ev.d_elope.bring_back.success: You caught up with the runaways at the second milestone. Everyone came home — and no one spoke.
ev.d_elope.bring_back.failure: You were too late: they had already married in the next town. Now it's too late — and everyone's hurt.
ev.d_elope.disown.ok: You forbade that name to be spoken in the house. At night you repeat it anyway.
ev.d_elope_later.title: Guests from the Road
ev.d_elope_later.text: A knock at the door: {npc} has come to show you {g=npc_sex:his|her} family — and a little one who looks at you with your own eyes. That long-ago elopement turned out to be the start of a strong household.
ev.d_disowned_return.title: At the Gate
ev.d_disowned_return.text: At the gate stands the one whose name hasn't been spoken in your house for many years. Time has done its work — a tired face, but the same eyes as in childhood. Asking forgiveness and leave to come in.
ev.d_disowned_return.open.ok: You stood holding each other for a long time, unable to say a word. Years of resentment melted away in one evening.
ev.d_disowned_return.shut.ok: You never went out. The footsteps beyond the gate faded, and the house grew even quieter.
ev.d_child_death.title: A Quiet House
ev.d_child_death.text: The fever came into the house suddenly. {npc} fought for three days, and on the fourth morning the house went very quiet. The toys still lie where they were left.
ev.d_child_death.vow: Make a vow to the gods
ev.d_child_death.vow.ok: You brought a small clay figure to the temple and asked the gods to keep your little one safe where the living cannot go.
ev.d_child_death.work: Don't stop for a single day
ev.d_child_death.work.ok: Your hands worked while your thoughts were far away. So the winter passed.
ev.d_child_death.together: Hold together with those close to you
ev.d_child_death.together.ok: You wept together and together remembered the funny things. Grief shared among everyone became a little easier to carry.
ev.d_child_betrayed.title: With a Bundle
ev.d_child_betrayed.text: {npc} stands on the doorstep with a bundle: {g=npc_sex:his wife|her husband} has been unfaithful — the whole street knows already. 'Can I stay with you?'
ev.d_child_betrayed.take_in: Take {g=npc_sex:him|her} in and see what happens
ev.d_child_betrayed.take_in.ok: The old room is occupied again. In the evenings you sit together for a long time — as you once did, long ago.
ev.d_child_betrayed.reconcile: Persuade {g=npc_sex:him|her} to go back and make peace
ev.d_child_betrayed.reconcile.success: You went to see both of them and talked to each separately. The marriage held — cracked, but it held.
ev.d_child_betrayed.reconcile.failure: It was too late to make peace. {npc} came back to you a month later — for good, and resentful of your advice.
ev.d_child_betrayed.confront: Go and have it out with the offender
ev.d_child_betrayed.confront.success: You said everything you thought, before witnesses. The shame fell where it belonged.
ev.d_child_betrayed.confront.failure: The talk ended in a brawl and a night with the watch. The shame went to you.
ev.d_illegit.title: A Basket at the Gate
ev.d_illegit.text: At dawn a basket with a baby was found at the gate, and a wax tablet: 'This child is yours. Remember that spring?' {npc} read the tablet before you did.
ev.d_illegit.take_in.ok: You lifted the baby from the ground — by custom, that means acknowledging the child as yours. {npc} wouldn't look at you for a week.
ev.d_illegit.temple: Take the child to the temple
ev.d_illegit.temple.ok: The priests promised to find good people. You walked away without looking back — and you're still looking back.
ev.d_illegit.nurse: Find a wet nurse and pay in secret
ev.d_illegit.nurse.ok: Every month you take a few coins to a wet nurse on the edge of town. {npc} pretends not to know where they go.
ev.d_illegit_grown.title: Familiar Eyes
ev.d_illegit_grown.text: A youth of about fifteen has sought you out — with your eyes and your habit of frowning. The baby from the basket at the gate. He asks for nothing; he only wants you to know who he is.
ev.d_illegit_grown.acknowledge: Embrace him and acknowledge him openly
ev.d_illegit_grown.acknowledge.ok: Let them talk. You introduced him to the neighbors by name — and for the first time he smiled.
ev.d_illegit_grown.help.ok: You gave him money for tools and arranged an apprenticeship with a master. More than that you couldn't give.
ev.d_illegit_grown.deny.ok: He gave you a long look and left. You stood on the threshold for a long time.
ev.d_drowning.title: Never Came Back
ev.d_drowning.text: {npc}, your friend, went down to the river in the morning — and never came back. The current that day was stronger than usual.
ev.d_drowning.text.athens: {npc}, your friend, set off in a boat for Aegina — and never came back. The squall came out of nowhere.
ev.d_drowning.funeral.ok: You arranged everything properly: mourners, offerings, a coin for the ferryman. That's what friends do.
ev.d_drowning.family: Look after the family left without a provider
ev.d_drowning.family.ok: You bring them grain and oil until the children grow up. You promised that at the funeral pyre.
ev.d_drowning.grieve.ok: You sit for hours on the shore where you once argued about trifles. Now there's no one to argue with.
ev.d_friend_family_thanks.title: A Debt of Memory
ev.d_friend_family_thanks.text: The children of your lost friend have grown up. One of them, a grown craftsman now, came with a gift: 'You didn't let us go under. Now it's my turn.' You've gained a new friend.
ev.d_friend_sudden.title: So Suddenly
ev.d_friend_sudden.text: Only yesterday {npc} was joking with you at the baths, and today {g=npc_sex:he is|she is} gone. The heart, the physicians say. You never finished talking about something important.
ev.d_friend_sudden.eulogy: Speak a farewell at the pyre
ev.d_friend_sudden.eulogy.ok: You spoke of the jokes, the long arguments, the way {npc} knew how to listen. People wept and smiled at the same time.
ev.d_friend_sudden.quiet.ok: You came to the tomb at dawn, when no one else was there, and finished saying everything you hadn't had time to say.
ev.d_friend_sudden.live: Stop putting life off until later
ev.d_friend_sudden.live.ok: That same month you did what the two of you had only ever dreamed about. {g=npc_sex:He|She} would have approved.
ev.d_sib_accident.title: The Fallen Scaffold
ev.d_sib_accident.text: {npc} {g=npc_sex:was working on a building site|had brought lunch to a building site} when the scaffolding collapsed. The contractor spreads his hands: the timbers were rotten, but who could have known.
ev.d_sib_accident.demand.success: The contractor had to pay. Money brings nothing back — but he won't buy rotten timber again.
ev.d_sib_accident.demand.failure: The contractor had friends among the judges. You lost both time and money.
ev.d_sib_accident.household.ok: There are a few more mouths at your table now. It's crowded — but it's right.
ev.d_sib_accident.let_go: Make an offering and let go
ev.d_sib_accident.let_go.ok: You brought wine and honey to the gods below and asked them to be merciful.
ev.d_sib_betrayal.title: The House Sold Behind Your Back
ev.d_sib_betrayal.text: You've learned that {npc} secretly sold the family house — without asking you, on a forged deed. The money, they say, is already spent.
ev.d_sib_betrayal.court.success: The court ruled the deed a forgery, and you got your share back. There's no kinship between you anymore — only the verdict.
ev.d_sib_betrayal.court.failure: The signature was ruled genuine. You lost both the house and the money spent on the case.
ev.d_sib_betrayal.forgive: Forgive — blood is thicker than water
ev.d_sib_betrayal.forgive.ok: All you said was: 'Pay me back someday.' {npc} couldn't raise {g=npc_sex:his|her} eyes.
ev.d_sib_betrayal.break.ok: You no longer come to family festivals. If {npc} walks in one door, you walk out the other.
ev.d_sib_repays.title: The Debt Repaid
ev.d_sib_repays.text: {npc} came with a heavy purse: 'This is for the house. I saved it coin by coin all these years.' For the first time in ages, you sat down at the table together.
ev.d_sib_deathbed.title: The Last Message
ev.d_sib_deathbed.text: A messenger brought word: {npc} is gravely ill and asking for you. You haven't spoken in many years.
ev.d_sib_deathbed.go.ok: You made it in time. You held hands and talked about childhood, not about the house. Towards morning {npc} passed away — peacefully, with no grudges.
ev.d_sib_deathbed.stay.ok: You didn't go. A week later a second message came — the last one. Pride turned out to be poor comfort.
ev.d_brother_war.title: A Different Person
ev.d_brother_war.text: {npc} has come back {g=npc_sex:from the war|from long wanderings in foreign lands} a completely different person: flinching at every knock, sleepless at night, hardly speaking of what {g=npc_sex:he|she} saw.
ev.d_brother_war.take_in.ok: You gave up the best room and ask no questions. Some nights you simply sit side by side by the hearth.
ev.d_brother_war.work.success: Working with the hands proved the best medicine. Six months later {npc} laughed for the first time.
ev.d_brother_war.work.failure: The work didn't take. In the evenings {npc} goes to the tavern more and more and comes back at dawn.
ev.d_brother_war.leave: Give it time and stay out of it
ev.d_brother_war.leave.ok: You decided not to pry. Maybe that's right — and maybe not.
ev.d_brother_heals.title: The Warmth Returns
ev.d_brother_heals.text: Years later {npc} began to talk about what had happened out there, far away. Talked for a long time — and then, for the first time in years, slept peacefully. You sat close by until dawn.
ev.d_t_sib_captive.title: The Ransom
ev.d_t_sib_captive.text: A letter came from the harbor: the ship {npc} was sailing on has been taken by pirates. The ransom is five hundred coins by the end of summer, or the captives will be sold at a slave market somewhere across the sea.
ev.d_t_sib_captive.pay.ok: You counted out the silver to the last coin. A month later {npc} stepped ashore — thin, sunburnt, but free.
ev.d_t_sib_captive.borrow.ok: The moneylender smiled too broadly. But {npc} is home, and you'll manage the debt somehow.
ev.d_t_sib_captive.haggle.success: The go-between cut the price in half. Pirates like quick money too.
ev.d_t_sib_captive.haggle.failure: The pirates took the haggling as an insult. The ship sailed, and no one heard of {g=npc_sex:him|her} again.
ev.d_t_sib_captive.cannot: There's no such money and never will be
ev.d_t_sib_captive.cannot.ok: You went to everyone you knew but couldn't raise it. Summer ended. You still peer at every sail.
ev.d_sib_lost_news.title: News from Across the Sea
ev.d_sib_lost_news.text: A visiting merchant says that in a distant port he saw a shop kept by former captives who had bought their freedom. One face there struck him as strangely familiar: the very image of yours.
ev.d_sib_lost_news.travel.success: You knew that face from the doorway. You couldn't let go of each other for a long time — so many years!
ev.d_sib_lost_news.travel.failure: The shop was closed, its owners gone who knows where. You came home empty-handed — but with hope.
ev.d_sib_lost_news.letter: Send a letter with the merchant
ev.d_sib_lost_news.letter.ok: You wrote only a few lines. An answer may take years — but now there's something to wait for.
ev.d_sib_lost_news.let_be.ok: You thanked the merchant and gazed at the sea for a long time. Whoever that person is, may all go well for them.
ev.d_t_bondage.title: The Bond
ev.d_t_bondage.text: Under the terms of a loan, {npc} is now bound to serve in the creditor's household until every last drachma is worked off. The nome scribe merely shrugs: the papers are in order.
ev.d_t_bondage.pay.ok: You laid the silver before the creditor and took the contract. It was torn up right there, before witnesses.
ev.d_t_bondage.petition.success: The strategos read the petition and judged the terms extortionate. {npc} came home that same day.
ev.d_t_bondage.petition.failure: The petition lay in the office for half a year and came back refused. The scribes had to be paid for every line.
ev.d_t_bondage.share.ok: You took on half the work yourself: after your own field, the creditor's. Your back aches, but the term is halved.
ev.d_t_bondage.leave: Everyone answers for their own debts
ev.d_t_bondage.leave.ok: {npc} didn't say a word to you as {g=npc_sex:he was|she was} led away.
ev.d_bonded_free.title: The Debt Worked Off
ev.d_bonded_free.text: {npc} has come home: the debt is worked off, the contract torn up. Calloused hands, a harder look — but free.
ev.d_t_father_family.title: The Second Family
ev.d_t_father_family.text: At the market in a nearby town you bumped into a youth with your father's chin and your father's walk. A few questions made everything clear: for years {npc} has been living in two households, and here he has a second family.
ev.d_t_father_family.confront.success: {npc} was silent for a long time, then wept — for the first time you can remember. You didn't forgive, but you understood.
ev.d_t_father_family.confront.failure: He said it was none of your business and slammed the door. Since then you speak only of the weather.
ev.d_t_father_family.accept.ok: You came to them with gifts. The youth was embarrassed, then shook your hand firmly: one more kinsman in the world.
ev.d_t_father_family.secret.ok: You haven't said a word to anyone. But the secret is heavy — you feel it even in your sleep.
ev.d_t_father_family.expose.ok: You told the family everything. There was shouting, there were tears, and {npc} spent a week sleeping at friends' houses.
ev.d_father_will.title: The Will
ev.d_father_will.text: After the funeral a young man from that second family came to you — with a will leaving him a third of everything. Now everyone will know your secret.
ev.d_father_will.honor: Honor the will of the departed
ev.d_father_will.honor.ok: You gave the young man his third and invited him to the memorial meal. A last wish is law.
ev.d_father_will.contest.success: The judges found the will improperly drawn. The young man got only a small share.
ev.d_father_will.contest.failure: The will was upheld, and the lawsuit ate part of your own inheritance.
ev.d_father_will.settle.ok: You divided everything at one table, without judges. The young man was more honest than you feared.
ev.d_mother_sudden.title: A Quiet Passing
ev.d_mother_sudden.text: Your mother {npc} was baking flatbread and grumbling at the neighbors' hens only this morning, and by evening she was gone. Quietly, without suffering — as if she'd just sat down to rest.
ev.d_mother_sudden.grand.ok: Mourners, flutes, a memorial feast for the whole street. She'd have liked it — though she'd have grumbled it cost too much.
ev.d_mother_sudden.modest: A modest farewell among your own
ev.d_mother_sudden.modest.ok: Only your own people, only her favorite songs. It felt more honest that way.
ev.d_mother_sudden.loom: Keep her loom and her work
ev.d_mother_sudden.loom.ok: You sat at her loom and clumsily continued the pattern she had begun. The thread still seems warm in your hands.
ev.d_parent_care.title: When Parents Grow Old
ev.d_parent_care.text: Your mother {npc} has begun forgetting names and mixing up days. Yesterday she set off for a market that hasn't existed for twenty years and was found at the city gate. She can't be left alone anymore.
ev.d_parent_care.take_in.ok: You feed her with a spoon and answer the same questions for the hundredth time. Sometimes she calls you by another name — and sometimes she looks at you as she did when you were little.
ev.d_parent_care.hire.ok: A kind woman from the next quarter comes every day. You visit in the evenings — and feel guilty, though you know you did the sensible thing.
ev.d_parent_care.relatives: Let the rest of the family look after her
ev.d_parent_care.relatives.ok: You send money and promise to visit. You promise often and visit rarely.
ev.d_parent_blessing.title: The Blessing
ev.d_parent_blessing.text: On the last evening {npc} suddenly knew you — clearly, as before. She stroked your head: 'You're a good {g:boy|girl}, you know.' And towards morning she quietly fell asleep forever.
ev.d_t_secret_birth.title: The Secret of Your Birth
ev.d_t_secret_birth.text: One night your mother {npc} confessed: you weren't born in this house. You were found as a baby on the temple steps and brought to a home that longed for a child. 'We loved you as our own. Forgive me for keeping silent.'
ev.d_t_secret_birth.seek: Search for those who left you
ev.d_t_secret_birth.seek.success: An old priest remembered that winter and named a village. Someone with your face lives there — your blood kin. You sat in silence for a long time, studying each other.
ev.d_t_secret_birth.seek.failure: You traveled half the country and spent a good deal, but the trail had long gone cold. You came home with nothing.
ev.d_t_secret_birth.stay: 'My mother is the one who raised me'
ev.d_t_secret_birth.stay.ok: You held her tight. Whose blood doesn't matter; what matters is whose hands rocked the cradle.
ev.d_t_secret_birth.anger.ok: You left, slamming the door. You've been lied to all your life — and there's no hiding from that thought.
ev.d_night_jail.title: A Night in Custody
ev.d_night_jail.text: {g:An argument in a tavern turned into a brawl|A quarrel with a market woman turned into a scuffle}, and you spent the night in custody on the straw among thieves and drunks. In the morning the magistrate decides what to do with you.
ev.d_night_jail.fine: Pay the fine and forget it
ev.d_night_jail.fine.ok: You paid and walked out into the sunlight. Your head is ringing, your purse lighter — a cheap lesson.
ev.d_night_jail.apologize.ok: You asked the injured party's forgiveness in front of everyone. Humiliating — but no fine.
ev.d_night_jail.argue: Argue that you didn't start it
ev.d_night_jail.argue.success: Witnesses backed you up, and the magistrate let you go in peace.
ev.d_night_jail.argue.failure: The magistrate didn't believe a word and doubled the fine — for insolence.
ev.d_record_haunts.title: An Old Case
ev.d_record_haunts.text: An old case surfaced at the worst possible moment: just before a profitable deal, your would-be partner learned you'd once been held in custody.
ev.d_record_haunts.honest: Tell it exactly as it happened
ev.d_record_haunts.honest.success: The partner listened and laughed: 'Who didn't brawl in their youth?' The deal went through.
ev.d_record_haunts.honest.failure: The partner listened politely — and found someone else.
ev.d_record_haunts.pay: Pay the gossip to keep quiet
ev.d_record_haunts.pay.ok: The one spreading rumors suddenly forgot everything. The deal is saved, but a bad taste remains.
ev.d_record_haunts.walk.ok: You left before being turned down. The past catches up — but doesn't always win.
ev.d_t_theft.title: A False Accusation
ev.d_t_theft.text: A purse of silver has gone missing from your neighbor's house, and he's pointing at you: you were seen at his door that very evening. The watch is already leading you to the magistrate, and a crowd is gathering behind you.
ev.d_t_theft.witnesses.success: Three neighbors swore you spent that whole evening at their festival. The accuser left red with shame.
ev.d_t_theft.witnesses.failure: The witnesses contradicted each other. The magistrate ordered you to repay the loss twice over, and now a thief's reputation follows you.
ev.d_t_theft.pay_off: Pay the accuser to drop it
ev.d_t_theft.pay_off.ok: The neighbor took the money and withdrew the charge. 'Paid up — must be guilty,' they whisper behind your back.
ev.d_t_theft.real_thief.success: You tracked down a lame water carrier trying to sell the silver to a money changer. The neighbor apologized publicly and paid for the insult.
ev.d_t_theft.real_thief.failure: You spent a week searching and found nothing. The court decided you were just stalling.
ev.d_t_theft.flee: Flee the city while you can
ev.d_t_theft.flee.ok: You left at night, taking only what you could carry. Now your name is on the list of fugitives.
ev.d_t_publican.title: The Tax Farmer
ev.d_t_publican.text: A tax farmer turned up with a scribe and a document: according to his records you've underpaid your taxes for three years, and with penalties it comes to three hundred coins. The records have clearly been doctored — but just try to prove it.
ev.d_t_publican.pay: Pay to be rid of him
ev.d_t_publican.pay.ok: You counted out the silver through gritted teeth. The tax farmer grunted with satisfaction — and marked you down as 'compliant.'
ev.d_t_publican.court.success: You brought your receipts for all three years to court. The forgery came to light, and the tax farmer had to apologize.
ev.d_t_publican.court.failure: The judge dined with the tax farmer on feast days. You lost — and paid even more.
ev.d_t_publican.bribe.success: For a few coins the scribe 'found an error' in his own records. The debt vanished as suddenly as it had appeared.
ev.d_t_publican.bribe.failure: The scribe turned out more honest than you thought — or more cowardly. Now a bribery charge has been added to the debt.
ev.d_t_publican.neighbors: Rally the neighbors — he's fleecing them too
ev.d_t_publican.neighbors.success: Half the quarter came to the magistrate with identical complaints. The tax farmer was recalled, and now you're invited to every assembly.
ev.d_t_publican.neighbors.failure: The neighbors nodded, but nobody went to the magistrate. You were left alone against the tax farmer — and he remembered.
ev.d_t_debt_prison.title: Debtors' Prison
ev.d_t_debt_prison.text: The creditor ran out of patience and got his way: you're held in custody until the debt is paid. Through the bars you can see the sky — and nothing else.
ev.d_t_debt_prison.text.rome: The creditor ran out of patience: by the court's ruling he may lead you away to his house and hold you until the debt is worked off. Through the bars you can see the sky — and nothing else.
ev.d_t_debt_prison.sell.ok: The house, the tools, even your festival clothes went under the hammer. You're free — and penniless.
ev.d_t_debt_prison.work: Work off the debt for the creditor
ev.d_t_debt_prison.work.ok: For two years you toiled for the creditor from dawn to dusk. The debt is closed — your back still aches.
ev.d_t_debt_prison.friends: Appeal to friends or a patron
ev.d_t_debt_prison.friends.success: Friends chipped in, and a patron made up the rest. You walked free and swore to repay every coin.
ev.d_t_debt_prison.friends.failure: Everyone sympathized, but no one gave money. You had to hand over half of everything you had.
ev.d_t_debt_prison.wait.success: A month later the creditor, a superstitious old man, forgave the debt to fulfill a vow to the gods.
ev.d_t_debt_prison.wait.failure: Months in the damp ruined your health. In the end the creditor took half of everything you owned.
ev.d_chains.title: Chains
ev.d_chains.text: The old case has run its course: you've been convicted and sent to hard labor — to the quarries, in chains, among thieves and runaway slaves.
ev.d_chains.endure.ok: A year in the quarry. You came back a different person — with scarred hands and a habit of silence.
ev.d_chains.escape.success: On a foggy night you slipped away through a ravine. Now you're free — but outside the law.
ev.d_chains.escape.failure: You were caught on the second day. Runaways are shown no mercy here.
ev.d_chains.intercede.ok: Your friends reached the right people and spared no expense. The sentence was commuted to a fine — ruinous, but without chains.
ev.d_m_spouse_late.text: {npc} came home after dark again, clothes smelling of someone else's perfume. You didn't ask — but you lay awake a long time.
ev.d_m_grave.text: You brought wine and honey to the tomb by the road and told of everything that had happened that year. The wind rustled the grass — as if someone were listening.
ev.d_m_toy.text: Sorting through a chest, you found a little clay horse with a chipped ear. You held it in your palms a long time, then set it on the shelf — in the most visible spot.
ev.d_m_cold_feast.text: At the family festival {npc} pointedly sat at the far end of the table and never once looked your way.
ev.d_m_dice.text: Under the bed you found a little bag of dice. {npc} swears they're old, from youth. Somehow there are fewer coins in the purse.
ev.d_m_whisper.text: At the market they whisper behind your back: 'That's the one who spent a night in custody.' A trader counted your change twice, for some reason.
